To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cyclic adenosine-3′,5’-monophosphate increases α-methyl- D -glucosid accumulation in kidney cortex slices by increasing the initial rate of entry of α-methyl D -glucoid into cells.

dibutyryl cyclic AMP enhances α-methyl- D -glucosid accumulation by rat kidney cortex slices by increasing the initial entry rate and the intracellular steady-state concentration of α-methyl glucoside and by increasing the maximum velocity of α-methyl-D-glucose accumulation.

the effect of dibutyryl cyclic AMP on α-methyl- D -glucosid accumulation by kidney cortex tissue is not mediated by an increase in protein synthesis and that dibutyryl AMP enhances α-methyl- glucoside accumulation by increasing the initial entry rate into the cells as well as by increasing the intracellular steady-state concentration of α-methyl glucoside.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of action of N 6,2′- O- dibutyryl cyclic 3′, 5′-adenosine monophosphate on α-methyl- D- glucoside uptake by kidney cortical slices.
the mechanism of the effect of N6-2′-O-dibutyryl adenosine 5′-cyclic monophosphate (cyclic AMP) on α-methyl- D -glucosid (α-methyl-Glc) accumulation by kidney cortex.

the effect of N _{6} -2′-0-dibutyryl adenosine 2′,5′ cyclic monophosphate (DBcAMP) on the accumulation of the non-metabolized sugar α-methyl-d-glucoside (α-MG) by rat, rabbit, and human kidney cortical slices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dibutyryl cyclic AMP increases the maximum velocity ( V max ) of the α-methyl- D -glucosidase entry process.
N 6 -dibutyrate cyclic adenosine-3′,5-monophosphate enhances α-methyl- D -glucosides transport in rat kidney cortex slices by increasing the maximum velocity of the transport system.

cyclic adenosine-3′,5’-monophosphate increases the rate of entry of α-methyl-d-glucoside into the cell, the rate of intracellular accumulation, and the intracellular steady-state concentration of the sugar.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cyclic nucleotide causes a stimulation of the rate of entry of glucoside into cells, an increased intracellular concentration of the glucosidic substrate and a stimulation of the intracellular rate of phosphorylation of the substrate.
N 6 -dibutyrate cyclic AMP enhances the accumulation of α methyl D glucoside by kidney cortex slices by increasing the intracellular steady-state concentration of the sugar.

cyclic nucleotides enhance the entry of α-methyl glucoside by rat kidney cortex slices by increasing both the rate of entry of glucoside and the intracellular concentration at which the entry process reaches equilibrium.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the effect of cyclic AMP on α-methyl- D -glucosidase accumulation is not mediated by an increase in the number of transport sites but is due to a direct effect of cyclic AMP upon the transport process.
the cyclic nucleotide does increase the rate of entry of α-methyl d-glucoside into renal tubular cells, but the effect is not a simple one.
the effect of cyclic nucleotides on the glucoside accumulation process is similar to the effect of cyclic adenosine nucleotides on Na-K-activated adenosine triphosphatase.
